entries.title: Owner result (independently checked): w677 biased frog recurrence at 2649/10000 with an exact finite start
entries.statement: INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED PROOF, C10_finite_start_bootstrap v3; novelty unverified. For every integer d>=3, ordinary and self-similar one-sleeper frog models on the rooted d-ary tree are recurrent at original inward drift p=2649/10000=0.2649, with independent paths, uniform outward choices and uniform ordinary-root reflection. Put p_d=inf{p: ordinary FM(d,p,1) is recurrent} and S_3=sup_{d>=3}p_d, as in Mathews p.2; the proof implies S_3<=2649/10000. Its specific self-similar ternary PGF operator has newborn pi=883/3234 and continuation beta=2649/7351. Two thousand exact upward grid iterations with N=10000 and scale 2^50 certify T^2000 1<=g_20 on the full interval, then the analytic tail gives Tg_a<=g_(a+1/1000) for every a>=20. Published GTW lower coupling and Mathews fixed-original-drift degree monotonicity transfer recurrence. A separate expanded-operator replay and a fresh byte-identical reproduction pass locally. Reviewer an agent wrote PASS on this exact version in AUDITS_FROM_REVIEWER.tsv; novelty was not judged. Unbiased T3 p=1/4 and T4 p=1/5 remain open.
entries.proof_text: The ternary physical fixed-point PGF satisfies f=Tf. Monotonicity of the exact operator and convex chord interpolation let2000 upward-rounded rational iterations dominate T^2000 1 and certify continuous domination by g20(x)=exp(-20(1-x)), including the endpoint cell through its slope. The exact analytic tail proves Tg_a<=g_(a+1/1000) for every a>=20. Repeated fixed-point domination gives f(x)=0 for every x<1, hence almost-sure recurrence in the self-similar model. GTW loop-erasure domination and Mathews degree coupling at the same original drift transfer this to every ordinary d>=3. The designated reviewer independently reran the rounded grid and checked the tail and published transfers.
assumptions: One active root frog and one sleeper per non-root vertex
Independent parent-probability 2649/10000 walks with uniform outward moves and root reflection
Published GTW lower coupling/fixed point and Mathews degree monotonicity

Hand: the substitution A=u, C=ut, B=ut^2 (u=exp(-a beta z), t=exp(-a gamma)) gives R=c1 e^{a(1-beta)z}+c2 e^{a(1-2beta)z}+c3 e^{-a eta z} with c3 needing 2K=L+J, sum c_i=L=1-pi z; case x<=1/2 (the c2 exponent is -a(beta+(2gamma-beta)x)<=-a beta) and case x>=1/2 (bracket 1-pi z+c1(e^{2a beta z}-1)+c2(e^{a beta z}-1), exponents -a(1-2beta), -a(1-3beta/2), K(a) decreasing in a) re-derived; T g_a<=g_{a+1/1000} then iterates to f=0 on [0,1). Reviewer's own code (reviewer_audits/t127/audit_c10_upper.py, nothing imported, own rounding: chord of h at each composition point rounded up, exact T on the upper triple rounded up, cap at S, running max) re-ran the 2000-step upper iteration from h_0=S: every tail cell i<=N-2 has h_2000(i+1)/S below the rigorous (mpmath interval) lower end of exp(-20(1-i/N)), final-cell slope >=20; exact Taylor partial sums give exp(10eta)>2, exp(20beta)>1000, exp(20(1-2beta))>100, exp(20(1-3beta/2))>1000; 4270601/4851000<999/1000 and eta-K>=43480527/566027000>=1/20 exactly as claimed. Same model check (asked for in the T127 dossier): C10 v3 and C12 v1 use the identical GTW ternary single-entry self-similar operator (1) with the identical parameter map pi=2p/(3-4p), beta=p/(1-p), gamma=(1-beta)/2, q=(1-pi)/3 (reviewer re-derived both fraction sets), the same map C4 v3's PASS checked against GTW (6)-(8) symbolically and by frog-by-frog simulation. Reviewer's float iteration (t127/float_sanity.py) shows a saddle-node: at p=0.2648 T^n 1 converges to a nontrivial fixed point with slope 1.366 at x=1 (C12's bound 1.407 sits above it), at p=0.2649 it collapses to 0 within 500 steps. So the self-similar model's critical drift lies in (0.2648, 0.2649], consistent with both claims; the SFM bootstrap cannot reach p=1/4 on T3 (target 1 of the dossier is forced). Transfers (GTW Prop 1.4, Mathews Thm 2) are the ones C4 v3's PASS accepted. Kind: bound (S_3<=0.2649), not a row move. Novelty not judged.

entries.title: Owner result (independently checked): w677 ternary self-similar frog transience at 331/1250, finite return mean
entries.statement: INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED PROOF, C12_self_similar_transience v1; novelty unverified. In the single-entry self-similar model on the rooted ternary tree, one active root frog and one sleeper per non-root vertex, at original p=331/1250=0.2648, newborn inward probability is 331/1213, continuing inward probability 331/919, and each eligible sibling probability 294/919. Downward frogs stay downward; stop root returns and every excess subtree entry. For returns V after the initial root departure the proof proves E[V]<=49510542141875/35184372088832<141/100, hence transience almost surely. The specific self-similar ternary PGF operator has an exact monotone polygon g with Tg>=g, g(1)=1 and finite left derivative. All 20772 affine-knot intervals pass rational quartic Bernstein positivity; a separate checker verifies exact coverage, knot exclusions and 103860 point identities, and a fresh run reproduces the leaf log. Finite cutoff PGFs satisfy T^n 1>=g, bounding their means; finite-time agreement and monotone convergence give the infinite-model mean bound. Node-only tests and a positive numerical fixed point are insufficient. This is one transient restricted-model case: no ordinary-model transience or critical-parameter lower bound follows without further comparison or parameter monotonicity. Reviewer an agent wrote PASS on this exact version in AUDITS_FROM_REVIEWER.tsv; novelty was not judged.
entries.proof_text: An exact monotone polygon g with Tg>=g and g(1)=1 is certified on all20772 affine-composition intervals by nonnegative rational quartic Bernstein coefficients. Operator monotonicity gives f_n=T^n1>=g for every finite cutoff. The endpoint quotient (1-f_n(x))/(1-x) is at most the finite polygon endpoint slope M, so E[V_n]<=M. Every time-K return count agrees with a cutoff n>K and is at most V_n; monotone convergence gives E[V]<=M<141/100. The reviewer independently rederived the operator derivatives and recomputed every exact polynomial piece. This transience statement concerns only the specified single-entry lower model.
assumptions: Rooted ternary tree, one active root frog and one sleeper per non-root vertex
GTW converted newborn pi=331/1213, upward continuation beta=331/919, sibling probability gamma=294/919
Downward frogs stay downward; stop root returns and excess subtree entries
V counts returns after initial root departure

relations.rationale: Both use the "specific self-similar ternary PGF operator" at different original drifts. "T^2000 1<=g_20" starts a recurrence bootstrap, while "Tg>=g, g(1)=1 and finite left derivative" bounds cutoff return means for a transient case. The directions differ, and the relation asserts no monotonicity in the drift.
